input: I am about to write the investment-case recommendation for the P1 review. The pre-pivot case promised break-even at month two to three and 8,818 dollars monthly net profit at month twelve, built on a removed pricing model and zero observed customers. The evidence now available is real but small: a working product verified end to end for both audiences, 23 verification-traffic billing rows showing the loop model's margins behave as designed, one founder-affirmed human use case, and no external traffic yet. My recommended reframe is to stage the investment case on evidence gates rather than projections: state observed unit economics as fact, state the cost base as fact, and gate each further outlay on adoption signals actually observed, with no month-twelve revenue claims at all. The risk I see is that an evidence-gated case may read as unambitious to the founder, who must also weigh personal runway and the lawyer engagement cost already committed. I believe honesty about the absence of demand evidence serves the founder better than a projection that inherits the old pack's confidence.
